Summary:
The Old World stands poised upon the razor's edge between annihilation and survival. Once more, the Twin-Tailed Comet streaks across the vaulted firmament; within the grand basilicas of the Cult of Sigmar, warrior-priests proclaim it as the God-King's stern gaze turning once again upon the mortal sphere, whilst upon the frozen northern Chaos Wastes, Chosen warlords revere it as the dark gods' irrevocable harbinger of final doom for the frail southern empires. The entire continent resembles an anvil clamped in the iron grasp of fate, where the great powers contest an unending struggle rooted in irreconcilable survival imperatives, spiritual covenants, ancestral claims, and governing doctrines.

The fundamental divide stems from the cosmic struggle between Chaos and Order. In the far north, the frontier of the Chaos Wastes steadily creeps southward; mutagenic winds spill ceaselessly from the shattered Polar Warp Gates, warping Norsca, the Troll Country, and the northern wastes into an expanding nightmare realm. Champions of Chaos, Daemon Princes, sorcerers, and warlike marauder tribes form the vanguard, their longships, warhounds, heavily armored warriors, and mutated monstrosities launching relentless incursions. The Imperial northern marches, the frozen steppes of Kislev, and the northern bastions of the World's Edge Mountains form civilization's desperate frontline against the encroaching dark.

In the heart of the Old World, the Empire of Man stands as humanity's greatest bulwark, maintained through the fragile trinity of steel, gunpowder, and faith, bound together by the Elector Count assembly. Newly crowned Emperor Karl Franz sits upon the throne of Altdorf, navigating an intricate labyrinth of provincial rivalries, clerical schisms, economic friction, and border defense. The wealth of Reikland and the unswerving loyalty of the Imperial State Troops are his bedrock, yet the fierce Cult of Ulric in Middenland perpetually questions Reikland's imperial mandate, Talabecland and Wissenland jealously guard regional prerogatives, Stirland and Ostland buckle under the dual terrors of Sylvania and northern raiders, while Nordland and Ostermark bleed their treasuries and levies along perilous coasts and eastern marshes. The Empire rests upon four grand pillars—the Council of Elector Counts, the Cult of Sigmar, the Imperial Colleges of Magic, and the Imperial Engineers and Gunnery Schools; if any pillar fractures, catastrophic collapse looms.

Beyond the Grey Mountains, the Kingdom of Bretonnia upholds a chivalric realm steeped in the divine mandate of the Lady of the Lake and the inviolable vows of the Knightly Code. From the grand court of Couronne, King Louen Leoncoeur commands the most devastating heavy lances in the Old World. Yet simmering peasant discontent, marauding greenskin raids, the cryptic isolationism of neighboring Athel Loren, and the encroaching shadows of Chaos continually test the realm's endurance. Louen must weigh the call of a glorious Errantry War to channel noble fervor and reaffirm the Lady's grace—whether northward into the Chaos-tainted wastes or south toward the arid Badlands, Bretonnia's chivalry faces unprecedented trials.

In the eastern march, the dread shadow of Sylvania refuses to lift. The Vampire Counts—heirs and scions of Vlad von Carstein—command nocturnal hosts of skeletal cohorts, shambling zombies, wights, and spectral abominations, patiently biding their time until the Empire falters. Rivalries among the midnight nobility rage fiercely: the proud von Carsteins, the martial Blood Dragon Knights, the reclusive Necrarch brotherhood, the ragged Strigoi ghouls, and the conspiratorial Lahmians all pursue separate schemes, whilst necromancers pour over forbidden grimoires of Nagash to summon primordial dread. Sylvanian serfs toil under bleak skies by day and bar their doors at dusk, well aware that their masters never truly perish.

Within the primeval forest of Athel Loren, the Asrai—Wood Elves—guard the oldest enchanted woodland in the world with peerless marksmanship and ancient, wrathful Treemen. Under Orion, the King in the Woods, and Ariel, the Mage Queen, the cycle of the Wild Hunt begins anew; woodsmen, greenskin warbands, Chaos marauders, and Imperial patrols who trespass beneath the canopy become quarry. Their fierce isolationism is forged from sacred pacts with the forest spirits and millennia of bitter betrayals.

Farther south and east across the arid expanses of the Badlands, the greenskin tribes spawn and multiply without end. Orc Warbosses and Goblin Shamans herd rival mobs into gathering hordes. The brutal idols of Gork and Mork, the feverish frenzy of the Waaagh!, and an inexhaustible sea of green flesh make them an unpredictable cataclysm, ever ready to wash over dwarf karaks, imperial marches, and bretonnian valleys alike.

Within the subterranean halls of the World's Edge Mountains, the ancient realm of Karaz Ankor fights a grim war of attrition. From the Throne of Power in Karaz-a-Karak, High King Thorgrim Grudgebearer reviews the ever-lengthening pages of the Dammaz Kron—the Great Book of Grudges. One ancestral hold after another has fallen to greenskins, Skaven, and nameless subterranean horrors; surviving redoubts depend on gromril plate, runic metallurgy, roaring cannons, and gyrocopters to maintain tenuous links. A dwarf never forgives a slight, but ancestral vengeance alone cannot reclaim lost mountain halls.

The continental economy strains under perpetual mobilization: Imperial gold crowns, Bretonnian silvers, and dwarfen runic ingots circulate through bustling hubs, yet trade routes are constantly disrupted by raiding. Grain, iron, timber, saltpetre, and thoroughbred warhorses have become prioritized strategic reserves, while luxury commerce yields to raw survival. The Winds of Magic remain an erratic and volatile tide: the arcane currents escaping the polar rifts empower the battle wizards of Altdorf's Colleges of Magic, but equally invigorate Chaos sorcerers, necromancers, and greenskin shamans. Imperial tolerance is tethered to strict licensing and military oversight, yet the peril remains ever-present: every mortal who channels the Winds opens a perilous door to the Ruinous Powers.

Thus stands the Old World: an Emperor weighing the bloody arithmetic of council edicts in Altdorf, a chivalric King plotting crusades in Couronne, vampires raising legions under Sylvanian mists, elven archers nocking warning shafts in Athel Loren, Chaos warlords mustering screaming hordes in the freezing north, orc warbosses bellowing beneath the scorched sun of the Badlands, and the Dwarfen High King somberly reciting new entries in the Book of Grudges. Any pitched battle, fallen lord, shattered host, or fallen citadel may radically upend the continental balance. The Twin-Tailed Comet traverses the heavens, and every scholar and sovereign watches its blazing trail—for it portends no idle omen, but the arrival of epochal upheaval. In the fateful weeks ahead, border casualties, logistical fluctuations, aristocratic parleys, village order, fief apportionments, and martial commands will continually accumulate into tangible shifts, shaping grand strategy, dynastic allegiances, and the fate of nations.
